Policy_Description: The scheme &quot;Yashwantrao Chavan Mukta Vasahat Yojana for VJNTs&quot; was launched by the Department of Social Justice &amp; Special Assistance, Government of Maharashtra. The scheme aims to enhance the quality of life of the Vimukta Jati and Nomadic Tribe (VJNT) families by developing sustainable income sources and promoting economic stability. Each family will receive a plot of land measuring 5 gunthas (approximately 500 square meters or about 5,382 square feet). This plot of land will include the construction of a 269-square-foot home as part of the assistance provided under the scheme.

Policy_Name: Yatra Anudan
Benefits_provided: - The Council provides travel grants to researchers and scientists to participate in international scientific workshops and other similar programs. | - Under this scheme, 50% of the travel expenses (up to a maximum of ₹25,000/-) are provided to researchers and scientists of the state.
Policy_Description: The scheme “Yatra Anudan” is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST) under the Science and Technology, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to support researchers and scientists in attending international scientific workshops and other similar programs by providing eligible applicants with travel grants covering up to 50% of the expenses (maximum ₹25,000/-).

Policy_Name: Yatra Pass in DTC non AC Buses for the Construction Workers
Benefits_provided: - A pass of 2400/- per three months for non AC DTC bus is provided.
Policy_Description: The "Yatra Pass in DTC non AC Buses for the Construction Workers" by the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Labour Department, Delhi, is a welfare scheme that provides a pass of ₹ 2400/- per three months for non AC DTC bus to the registered workers for purchasing. All types of bus passes i.e. Conventional Bus Pass as well as e-Bus Pass can be made online.

Policy_Name: Yoga Wellness Center
Benefits_provided: Under this scheme, Yoga, naturopathy, and counseling services are provided based on the individual’s health condition. For this, the OPD fee is ₹1.00 per person in rural areas and ₹2.00 per person in urban areas.
Policy_Description: The “Yoga Wellness Center” is implemented by the Ayush Department, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote holistic health and wellness among people of all age groups through yoga, naturopathy, and personalized counseling.

Policy_Name: Young Achievers Awards
Benefits_provided: Award Components: The Young Achievers Award consists of a memento, a Citation and a Cash Burse as fixed by Tiatr Academy of Goa. | Recognition Ceremony: Selected artistes are honoured at a special function on 16th November on the occasion of the Birth Anniversary of Regina Fernandes, the First Lady of the Tiatr Stage. | Annual Awards: The award is given to a male and a female artiste every year. | _*The selected artistes must be compulsorily present in person to receive the award._
Policy_Description: The scheme "Young Achievers Awards" was launched by the Tiatr Academy under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to recognize young talented artistes who have contributed and continue to work for the development of tiatr, its song and music, and have enriched Konkani Tiatr and Song through All India Radio, Doordarshan and other platforms at national and international levels. The scheme provides recognition through awards consisting of a memento, citation and cash burse, given to one male and one female artiste annually. The scheme also provides a special honour function held on 16th November on the occasion of the Birth Anniversary of Regina Fernandes, the First Lady of the Tiatr Stage.

Policy_Name: Young Innovators Program
Benefits_provided: The total amount of assistance provided under this scheme shall be subject to a maximum limit of ₹5,00,000/- One person can seek the assistance under this scheme only once for a particular innovation.
Policy_Description: Innovation may be defined as exploiting new ideas leading to the creation of a new product, process or service. It is not just the invention of a new idea that is important. It is actually “bringing it to market”, putting into practice and exploiting it in a manner that leads to new products, services or systems that add value or improve quality. It possibly involves technological transformation and management restructuring. Innovation also means exploiting modern technology and employing out-of-the-box thinking to generate new value and to bring about significant changes in society. Mission Youth under this program aims to enhance young people’s learning and development through a range of non-formal learning activities with focus on pioneers experimentation and innovation in education, entrepreneurship, art, research and cross-sectoral partnerships. ﻿ The major activities to be taken under this program are detailed as under: To support the innovative entrepreneurship Youth innovative entrepreneurship ideas contest Promotion of young social/ educational innovators Innovative initiatives in conservation/ management of resources ﻿ Objectives The broad aim of the Scheme is to empower youth of J&K to innovate new products, services or models in any area of their interest like art, craft, literature, science, etc. The endeavour is to facilitate promising innovators to exhibit their talent and excel in their areas of interest by providing them with institutional support and financial assistance.

Policy_Name: Young Interns Program
Benefits_provided: Stipend | ₹ 30,000/- per month. | Laptop Connectivity and Mobility Support | ₹ 2500/- shall be paid to each intern per month. | Leaves | Every intern will be eligible for one casual leave every month on an accrual basis. Such leaves shall be provided in a cumulative manner i.e. 12 leaves for the entire year (from January to December).
Policy_Description: The Young Interns Program (YIP) is an internship program, envisaged by the Government of Rajasthan, for providing opportunities for talented and progressive youth to upgrade their skills by gaining practical experience working in programs, schemes and projects of the government departments. The program is mutually beneficial to the government as well as the interns: | - The Government is benefitted by infusing novelty and innovation in the project implementation and service delivery system through the youthful and courageous ideas & techniques of the young interns. 1. The Interns are benefitted by attaining knowledge of project implementation and the ecosystem of the government functionalities.  |  > Objectives | - To empower the young brains to attain awareness and knowledge about various government programs and services and about various interventions between government, service providers, recipients and peripheral agencies such as media, civil society etc. | - To strengthen their research and evaluation skills in the field of public administration and development services. | - To generate interest amongst the youth towards the entire service delivery ecosystem of the public services. | - To get independent critical analysis of government programs and for seeking suggestions for corrective measures. | - To augment innovations from the young minds to enhance the outreach and impact of government schemes &amp; programs. | Deployment | For FY 2023-24, the following arrangements for the deployment of 300 young interns may be executed: | - Interns to be deployed at each Divisional HQ: 3 each (7x3=21) | - Interns to be deployed at each District HQ: 2 each (26x2=52) | - Interns to be deployed at the Department level for specific to the schemes/projects/programs: 227 (300-21-52=227) | Duration | - The internship is of one-year duration. | NOTE 1: After the end of the first year, if the mentor/nodal officer feels and recommends the extension in the internship duration on the basis of the performance of the intern, the duration of the internship may be increased by one more year with six months at a time. | NOTE 2: In no circumstances, the duration of the internship shall be more than two years.

Policy_Name: Young Investigators Programme in Biotechnology
Benefits_provided: - Young Scientists without fellowship/salary are eligible for a fellowship of ₹45,000/- plus 10% HRA per month, in addition to the support for travel, contingency, consumables, and minor equipment. | - A Principal Investigator having a regular position can seek manpower. | - Maximum support up to ₹30 lakhs (excluding overhead charges @ 10% of the project cost subject to a ceiling of ₹ 1.0 lakh) for a period not exceeding three years.
Policy_Description: The programme “Young Investigator’s Programme in Biotechnology (YIPB)” is a research support programme that aims to provide quick research support to young researchers to pursue their ideas in newly emerging and front-line areas of research in Biotechnology. The scheme is implemented by Kerala Biotechnology Commission, KSCSTE to provide quick research support to young scientists to pursue their bright ideas in newly emerging and front-line areas of research in Biotechnology. Proposals can be submitted in any branch of biotechnology related to medical, agriculture, veterinary, environment, marine, industrial or bio-resources. Post-doctoral students/Research Associates not having permanent positions can also be Principal Investigator provided a senior faculty/scientist holding permanent positions shall associate as Co-Principal Investigator. A maximum research grant of ₹30 lakh will be provided to the selected projects for a maximum duration of 3 years. Grants will be paid for specific projects to cover expenditure on manpower, equipment, consumables, contingencies and travel.

Policy_Name: Youth Art Training Fellowship Scheme
Benefits_provided: - Monthly training fellowship of ₹10,000 per selected participant. | - Professional art training at government-recognized art and music institutions (Page No. 3).- Certification after successful completion of training. | - Opportunity to receive structured guidance in classical, tribal, and folk art forms. | - The fellowship is valid only for the approved training period of 3 months.
Policy_Description: The “Youth Art Training Fellowship Scheme" has been launched by the Department of Culture, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The scheme aims to promote interest and skill development among youth in various art forms such as music, dance, theatre, painting, and crafts. Under this scheme, monthly training fellowships are provided to selected young artists to support their artistic training.

Policy_Name: Youth Engagement through Empowered Youth Organisations (YESS)
Benefits_provided: - Financial assistance of up to INR 1.00 lakh per financial year may be sanctioned to eligible youth organisations or individuals. | - Up to 10% of the total applications may receive a higher amount of financial support.
Policy_Description: The Youth Engagement through Empowered Youth Organisations (YESS Meghalaya) scheme, under the Department of Sports and Youth Affairs, Government of Meghalaya, provides financial assistance to registered youth organisations and eligible individual youth to carry out activities that promote youth development. The scheme is designed to strengthen networking, collaboration, and meaningful community-level engagement. | Targeted Stakeholders | Financial assistance is extended to the following entities and individuals: | - Societies and Cooperatives | - Voluntary and Not-for-Profit Organisations | - Youth Clubs and Associations | - Socio-Cultural Clubs | - Alumni Associations | - Community-level Youth Institutions or Groups | - Individuals selected for competitions or events with valid proof of participation

Policy_Name: Youth Hostel Scheme
Benefits_provided: - Affordable accommodation: Youth hostels offer a much cheaper alternative to hotels and guesthouses.1. Social atmosphere: Youth hostels are a great place to meet new people from all over the world.1. Cultural experience: Youth hostels are often located in places of cultural interest, giving you the opportunity to learn about the local culture and traditions.1. Flexible options: Youth hostels offer a variety of accommodation options, including dormitories, private rooms, and family rooms. Policy_Description: The Youth Hostel Scheme is managed by the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports under the Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, Government of India. The Central Government provides financial assistance to the State Governments for the construction and maintenance of youth hostels. The State Governments are responsible for the day-to-day management of youth hostels.

Policy_Name: Youth and Eco Club
Benefits_provided: Under the Youth and Eco Club in schools, awareness programmes, competitions, and activities were organized on plastic reduction, kitchen gardening, tree plantation, environmental protection, waste management, cleanliness, and water conservation, etc. | - Bagless Day and Environment Friendly Awareness. | - Awareness Through Skits and Plays. | - Poster makings, Paintings, Slogan writing etc. Competition and "Say No" to Single Use plastic. | - Cleaning Drives of the School and Surrounding and Keeping Toilets Usable. | - Composting Food Waste in the School. | - Planting of Trees in Schools.
Policy_Description: The scheme “Youth and Eco Club” is implemented under the Samagra Shiksha Programme by the Secondary Education Department, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote environmental awareness and sustainable practices among students by organizing programmes and activities such as plastic reduction initiatives, kitchen gardening, etc. along with various competitions to engage and empower students in protecting the environment.

Policy_Name: Yuva Srujan Puraskar (Navsarjan Chetana Puraskar)
Benefits_provided: - A memento, certificate of appreciation and financial purse to the extent of ₹ 25,000/- per individual.1. Every year a maximum of 6 persons in the fields of Music/Dance, Drama/Tiatr, Folk Art, Photography/Painting, Craft, Sculpture, Bhajan/Kirtan, Literature, and Film shall be considered.
Policy_Description: The scheme "Yuva Srujan Puraskar (Navsarjan Chetana Puraskar)" by the Directorate of Art and Culture, Government of Goa is designed to honour the young Goan individuals who have excelled in the field of Art and culture in Goa. The scheme intends to give recognition to young artists par excellence for their outstanding achievements and for their extraordinary contribution to the field of Art and culture. | Objectives | - To honour the young artists for their contribution towards the field of Goan Art and culture. | - To felicitate the young artists par excellence for their outstanding achievement in the respective field of their art. | - To recognize, encourage and identify the young artists as Youth Artists of the State.

Policy_Name: Yuvak Mangal Dal and Mahila Mangal Dal Swavalamban Yojana
Department: Department of Youth Welfare and Provincial Protection Corps
Benefits_provided: Under this scheme, financial assistance of ₹14,268/- is provided to purchase essential materials for community use, aimed at making the Mangal Dals self-reliant.
Policy_Description: The scheme “Yuvak Mangal Dal and Mahila Mangal Dal Swavalamban Yojana” was launched by the Department of Youth Welfare and prantiy rakshak dal (PRD), Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote self-reliance among village-level male and female youth groups (Mangal Dals) by providing financial support for the purchase of essential materials, enabling them to become self-reliant and undertake community-based activities.

Policy_Name: Yuvasree Prakalpa
Benefits_provided: Cash Benefits: Subject to fulfillment of the aforesaid eligibility criteria an individual may receive unemployment assistance under the scheme ₹ 1500/- per month. Job Seeking: By registering in Employment Bank, beneficiaries can search and apply for jobs per their skills. Training Program: The recipient can upgrade his/her skill subsequently under any of the Skill Development programs of the state government / private training institutes and increase his/her employability. The training program shall include soft skills training, basic IT training, basic communication training, and other skill as per the need or the interest of the beneficiary. Placement Support : Assistance in placing the candidate in a Government or Private organization. ﻿ ﻿ ﻿ ﻿
Policy_Description: 'Yuvasree' (earlier named as "Yuva Utsaha Prakalpa") was launched by the Labour Department, Govt. of West Bengal, with effect from 1st October 2013. The objective of the scheme is to provide unemployment assistance to the enrolled jobseekers of the Employment Bank to enable them to upgrade their level of skill in order to make them employable or suitable for setting up of self-employment ventures.

Policy_Name: Zero Budget Natural Farming
Benefits_provided: - A subsidy of 50% provides to farmers to buy the farming items. | - A large drum of 200 litres, a small drum of 50 litres capacity, a bucket of 20 litres capacity, a Jug, filter, water spray, sprayer, Trichoderma, cow-urine, dung, etc. Material and organic mulch material like leaves of trees, weed bedding, leaves of millet-sorghum, etc., groundnut peels, and in the field for moisture conservation between the rows, 50% of the total cost of available other waste material or a maximum of Rs.600/- per farmer will be given as subsidy by DBT. | - Training and Farmers Tours. | - Gram Panchayat level Training.
Policy_Description: Zero Budget Natural Farming is natural farming based on cow-products (cow urine, dung) produced by indigenous cows. All agricultural inputs are prepared by the farmer from his own farm, no inputs are purchased from the market. Therefore, he does not have to spend anything directly. Due to which it is called zero budget based farming. At present, reducing the indiscriminate use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides and irrigation. To reduce the cost of agriculture, improve the quality of agricultural products and increase production per acre. Use of Beejamrit for treatment of seeds and Dravjeevamrit and Ghanjeevamrit etc. for nutrition. Use of Neemastra, Brahrastra and Aagnestra for the prevention of insects.  |  Objective:- | - To promote environment-protected and climate-tolerant natural farming practices so that the fertility power of the land can be increased. | - To reduce the cost of cultivation by less irrigation, sustainable and integrated organic methods so that farmers can get more income per unit area. | - Production of chemical free and nutritious food for human health and wellness. | - Protecting biodiversity and environment. | - Empowering farmers for production, processing and progress by developing them in the form of clusters / groups. | - To make farmers entrepreneurs for marketing and by connecting directly with the national market.

Policy_Name: Zero Ticket Bus Travel Scheme for Women

Policy_Description: The Zero Ticket Bus Travel Scheme. The fact that more than 48% of women users are more than 40 years of age indicates the extent to which this scheme benefits older women. They comprise almost 44% of the sample users

Policy_Name: Zupda Vijlikaran Yojana
Benefits_provided: - Free electricity household connection is provided to BPL/Lower income group beneficiary.
Policy_Description: The “Zupda Vijlikaran Yojana” was launched by the Energy and Petro Chemicals Department, Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to provide access to electricity for Below Poverty Line (BPL) and low-income families across the state. Under this scheme, free household electricity connections are provided to eligible families.

Policy_Name: e-Adhigam Scheme - Free Tablet
Benefits_provided: Tangible Benefits: | - Free Android Tablets – Provided to students in Classes 8 to 12.1. Pre-loaded Content – Tablets come with pre-loaded educational content, personalized adaptive learning (PAL) platform, and study materials.1. 2GB Free Data Per Month – Enables students to access online study resources. | Mode of Disbursement: | - Tablets are distributed in government schools under the Haryana Free Tablet Scheme. | Frequency of Disbursement: | - Tablets are distributed once to eligible students. | - Free 2GB of data is provided every month. | Validity of Benefits: | - The tablets remain the property of the Haryana Government. | - Students must return the tablets after completing Class 12.

Upon passing Class 12, students will have to return it for online education. | Expected Time of Disbursement: | - In Phase 1, 5 lakh tablets were distributed to Class 10 and 12 students. | - Tablets for Class 11 students are distributed after Class 10 board exams. | - Tablets for Classes 8 and 9 will be provided in a phased manner.

Policy_Name: scholarship scheme - Uttarakhand Agricultural Production & Marketing Board, Uttarakhand
Benefits_provided: Students pursuing courses in Agriculture, Forestry, Fisheries, Horticulture and other related fields at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar; R.M.P. (P.G.) College, Gurukul Narsan, Haridwar; V.C.S.G. Uttarakhand University of Horticulture and Forestry, Bharsar, Pauri Garhwal; and the College of Horticulture, V.C.S.G. Benefits_provided: 1)  UGC will award 10,000 (ten thousand) fresh scholarships per year. 2)  ₹5,400/- per month for general degree courses and ₹7,800/- per month for technical/medical/professional/paramedical courses. 3)  The scholar would be awarded from the date of joining the course as certified by the University/Institution/ College. 4)  Scholarship (as certified by the institutions identified under this scheme) will be paid to the selected students by the UGC through DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) Mode and will be transferred to the Bank account of the beneficiaries. Policy_Description: A scholarship scheme by the Ministry of Education and the University Grants Commission. Taking special interest with regard to the promotion of higher education in the NER, i.e. for improving the GER, promoting higher education, and encouraging children belonging to the economically weaker sections of the NE region, the UGC has decided to launch “Ishan Uday” Special Scholarship Scheme for North Eastern Region from the academic session 2014-15. Before launching the scheme the UGC undertook wide-ranging consultations with State Governments and Central & State Universities of the NE region, the Ministry of, the Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region, the North Eastern Council, Shillong, and other stakeholders. The scholar would be awarded from the date of joining the course as certified by the University/Institution/ College. ﻿ The eligibility criteria are as follows - Students with the domicile of NER, whose parental annual income does not exceed ₹4,50,000 from all sources. Passed XII or equivalent in the preceding year of study i.e. 2021 for applications called for during the year 2021-22, and secured admission in the first year of any degree course. ﻿ OBJECTIVES 1) To provide equal opportunities for higher studies in NE Region. 2) To increase the Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in NE Region. 3) To focus more on professional education in NE Region. 4) Optimum utilization of NER Budgetary Allocation. ﻿ SCOPE Ten thousand (10,000) fresh scholarships every year for general degree courses, and technical and professional courses, including medical and paramedical courses as certified by the Registrar/ Principal/ Director of University/ College/ Institute.

Policy_Name: ₹ 5 Lakh Insurance Cover To Farmers
Policy_Type: Agriculture,Rural & Environment; Banking,Financial Services and Insurance
Benefits_provided: - Financial Security: Provides ₹5 lakh insurance coverage to farmers' families in case of the farmer's death, offering substantial financial assistance.	1. Inclusive Coverage: Covers death due to any cause, including natural causes and accidents.	1. Quick Disbursement: Ensures compensation is paid to the nominee within 10 days of the farmer's death.	1. Zero Cost to Farmers: Farmers are not required to pay any premium, as the state government bears the entire cost on their behalf.	1. Wide Beneficiary Base: Approximately 50 lakh farmers benefit from this scheme annually.
Policy_Description: Launched on 15 August 2018, the scheme "₹5 Lakh Insurance Cover for Farmers" is an Insurance Scheme by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Telangana. This scheme provides ₹5 lakh insurance coverage to all farmers aged between 18 and 60 years, ensuring financial security for their families in case of the farmer's death, irrespective of the cause. The nominee receives the compensation within 10 days of the farmer's death. The state government pays an annual premium of nearly ₹500 crore on behalf of around 50 lakh farmers to the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), and farmers do not need to pay a single rupee. The scheme is being implemented by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).
